A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 21-page paper, including Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the scientific text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are fully comparable.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original GCTM experiments in Section 5 and Appendix E, including image generation, translation, restoration, editing, and ablation results.

after.justification: v4.pdf retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix E, including quantitative evaluations in Tables 1–5 and qualitative demonstrations.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1–5 are unchanged, including the GCTM objectives, independent/optimal-transport/supervised couplings, Gaussian perturbation, and restoration and editing procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR10, Edges→Shoes, Night→Day, Facades, FFHQ, and ImageNet. The generation, translation, restoration, editing, and latent-manipulation scenarios are identical, including the high-resolution restoration evaluation in Appendix E.3.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments: CTM/CM/iCM for generation; regression, Pix2Pix, Palette, and I2SB for translation; DPS/CM and supervised baselines for restoration; and BBDM/EGSDE in Appendix E.1.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A and E retain identical split descriptions, resolutions, sample counts, metrics, training settings, inference-step budgets, and timing procedures.

E4.justification: The coupling comparison in Section 5.1, Gaussian-perturbation and sigma-max ablation in Section 5.6, latent-manipulation demonstrations, and editing-time analysis in Appendix E.2 are unchanged. The supplementary qualitative examples are also identical.

E5.justification: The tables, learning curves, and appendices retain identical statistical reporting. There are no changes to run-count or seed disclosures, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and all result figures contain identical values, curves, and qualitative outputs. For example, one-step GCTM FID remains 5.32 on CIFAR10 and 40.3 on Edges→Shoes.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2, mathematical definitions, ODE derivations, coupling formulations, and proofs in Appendix C are identical. No mathematical correction or additional formal result appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about generalizing CTMs to arbitrary distributions, explaining the design space, and enabling competitive one-step image manipulation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of coupling-related acceleration, restoration guidance, and the perception-distortion tradeoff are unchanged. Appendix D retains the limitation that unconditional generation has not reached state-of-the-art performance and the suggestion of further hyperparameter tuning.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain the same hyperparameters, network and solver details, evaluation implementations, and pseudocode. Appendix D preserves the same statements about supplementary experiment code and releasing code upon acceptance.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography entries, and positioning relative to CTMs, flow matching, and diffusion methods are unchanged. Some bibliography hyperlink annotations disappear, but no cited work is removed.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' to 'Preprint', and the arXiv stamp updates from v2 dated 7 October 2024 to v4 dated 21 July 2025. The body wording, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–14 and Tables 1–5 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. Rendered page bodies match throughout; the header and version-stamp text edits do not reorganize the layout.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, reproducibility details, and limitations are identical throughout the main text and Appendices A–E. The header, version metadata, and hyperlink annotation changes do not meaningfully improve or weaken the paper's overall quality.
